commenti.body: My friends at Far Afield, a UK clothing brand, have released a range of shirts inspired by cult classic films. They're all pretty loud, not really my usual vibe, but I'm tempted by the True Romance one nonetheless. Have done Raising Arizona, Back to The Future & Cape Fear also. Figured it was worth posting in here in case anyone was interested - [https://www.farafield.uk/collections/far-afield-pop](https://www.farafield.uk/collections/far-afield-pop)

Hi, I understand this is the thread where I can request recommendations?  
I'm looking for films that play with the boundaries between documentary and fiction.

I'm not talking about mockumentaries - more like cases when the director has a person playing themselves in a scripted scene that's based on an actual event from their lives, or similar stuff in that vein.

A few examples I'm already familiar with:

* Close-Up by Abbas Kiarostami
* Sans Soleil by Chris Marker
* Symbiopsychotaxiplasm: Take One by William Greaves
* Rolling Thunder Revue: A Bob Dylan Story by Martin Scorsese
* The Rider - Chloé Zhao

Would love to know of more good or at least interesting ones!

The latter two films in Kiarostami's Koker trilogy.

*Synecdoche, New York* for a more meta, in-universe example.

Have been flirting with wanting to blog for a bit, but I mostly never do it. Here is the link to a site I created 2 years ago where I've posted a whopping two reviews/essays. They are about Medicine For Melancholy, Barry Jenkins' first film and The Go-Between, a 1971 Joseph Losey film I watched last night for the first time.

I'd be willing to listen to feedback if you have any, so here it is (essentially no one has ever gone): https://catchinguponculture.blogspot.com/

I'm not trying to revolutionize review writing, but my original intent was to write about interesting generally older films (and sometimes other topics) and eventually do bigger essays regarding specific directors, eras, actors, etc.
Probably the OG example of this is *8 1⁄2,*
Jafar Panahi’s Taxi is the best

Agnes Varda flips around from fiction to documentary. Many of her feature films have documentary elements, and visa-versa. One of the best examples is Vagabond (1985). Maybe it's a French thing - there's also Laurent Cantet. His films usually have a social justice element and he uses real work environments and the real people who work in them. In his 2008 film The Class the lead actor is actually the teacher on who's experience the film is based - he's playing himself in his own story. I recently saw Bertrand Taverier's It All Starts Today (1999) which is about a school in a poor mining town. The leads are actors, but smaller parts are played by locals (basically playing themselves) and the school setting (including staff and pupils) is the actual school of the town.

Not a movie I see discussed a lot (if ever) but Jafar Panahi’s The Mirror from 97 fits your criteria perfectly and is woefully under seen. As for recent movies, I really really liked Bloody Nose, Empty Pockets.
